thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: INCIDENT 1832109876 detected — elevated 5xx rate and cross-region routing anomalies for redwood-api-prod. Symptoms: requests from EU routing to us-east causing 300-800ms tail latency and ~15% error rate. Affected endpoints: /v1/generate, /v1/chat. Auto-threshold triggered at 2026-03-15T08:11:16Z.

pagerduty: Paging @maria (network-oncall) and @ashley (eng-sre) — severity P1. Please acknowledge.

ashley (eng-sre): acked. I'm in. Currently seeing increased 503s in EU ingest logs and spikes in cross-region hops in traceroutes.

maria (network-oncall): I see BGP path changes to eu-west that prefer us-east via transit provider for a subset of prefixes. Could be route flap or policy change. Pulling up recent peer configs.

simon (eng-platform): Confirmed alerts on our routing-telemetry: region_pinning failures for route-policy 'geo-prefer' between eu-west-1 and us-east-1 started ~08:09Z. All canaries show healthy though — suggests partial scope.

james (prod-support): Getting customer reports: three customers on Dedicated reported timeouts and 1:1 support threads. CS wants an ETA for mitigation to share.

leo (infra): Reproduced traceroute from eu-west lambda -> model pool shows hop 4 diverting to us-east 1. Sample: ```traceroute to model-frontend (10.4.5.7), 30 hops max
 1 10.0.0.1 (10.0.0.1) 0.6 ms 0.5 ms 0.4 ms
 2 192.168.12.1 1.2 ms 1.0 ms 1.0 ms
 3 transit-asn 42.11 ms 40.9 ms 39.8 ms
 4 us-east-edge 120.5 ms 119.8 ms 121.2 ms
```

ashley (eng-sre): Looking at router metrics — BGP changes correlate with provider X announcing a more specific for our eu-west prefixes but propagated across regions. Possible mis-advert from provider edge.

maria (network-oncall): I'm opening a support case with provider X now. In parallel we should force pinning policy for eu-west customers to local edge to restore locality. Simon, can you flip the routing policy to strict-pin for prod eu-west?

simon (eng-platform): I can push a temporary policy override. Will do canary on 5% traffic first. Command I'm about to run: ```redwoodctl routing apply --scope prod --region eu-west-1 --policy strict-pin --canary 5```

ashley (eng-sre): Good. Add KV cache bypass for affected endpoints while we stabilize to avoid stale session redirects.

simon (eng-platform): Canary applied at 08:15:02Z. Monitoring metrics.

console-bot: Canary rollout complete (5% -> 5%). No errors in rollout.

maria (network-oncall): Provider case opened: ticket #PX-45219. Provider acknowledges potential mis-announcement, investigating internal edge config. Trying to get timeline.

leo (infra): Within 60s of canary applying, eu-west latency tail dropped ~220ms for canary. Error rate for canary hosts down from 14% -> 1.2%.

james (prod-support): CS: telling affected customers we have a mitigation in progress and rolling fix, ETA 15–30m, will follow up with postmortem.

ashley (eng-sre): Escalation note: we'll expand strict-pin to 100% if provider fix not confirmed in 20m. Need agreement: do we want auto rollback if errors increase?

maria (network-oncall): Agreed. I'll hold on manual expansion for now until provider confirms or rollback is needed. Keep canary at 5% and watch.

ops-runbooks-bot: Runbook 'cross-region-routing' recommends: 1) contact transit provider, 2) apply strict-pin, 3) enable local egress fallback, 4) notify CS. All steps in progress.

ashley (eng-sre): Observability note: enabling per-request traces for affected routes to get AS path. Doing that now (sampling bump x10).

simon (eng-platform): Rolling canary to 30% (08:21:12Z) — manual increase after positive signals. Command: ```redwoodctl routing scale --scope prod --region eu-west-1 --policy strict-pin --to 30```

console-bot: Canary scaled to 30%. No immediate anomalies.

maria (network-oncall): Provider updates: they see a config sync error causing more-specifics to leak from us-east into eu-west mesh. They estimate fix in ~10 minutes. Ticket updated.

leo (infra): Error rates dropping across eu-west apps correlated with strict-pin scaling: overall 5xx rate down from 15% -> 3% at 08:24Z. Latency tail back to ~60ms in most traces.

james (prod-support): Notifying customers: sending short note — mitigation in progress, partial traffic restored, next update in 15m. Customer-success drafting message.

customer-success: Draft for CS channel: "We're currently mitigating a cross-region routing issue affecting some EU traffic; we've applied a temporary routing policy to restore locality and are monitoring. No model state lost; we expect normal traffic within 30 minutes." Approving?

ashley (eng-sre): Approve and send. Also include pointer to status.redwood.ai with live metrics.

maria (network-oncall): Provider reports fix applied at 08:30Z and withdraw of leaked specifics. I'm watching BGP table convergence now.

leo (infra): BGP table shows normal prefixes again at 08:31:40Z. Traceroutes return to eu-west hops. Measured error rate now ~0.5% across region.

simon (eng-platform): Rolling strict-pin back to default policy with gradual canary 30% -> 0% to avoid flips: ```redwoodctl routing scale --scope prod --region eu-west-1 --policy strict-pin --to 0 --grace 120```

console-bot: Rollback started at 08:33:10Z. Monitoring for regressions.

ashley (eng-sre): Observability: traces show stable AS paths and no cross-region jumps. No increased errors after rollback start.

maria (network-oncall): Confirming provider closed ticket #PX-45219 at 08:35Z — they fixed configuration propagation bug. Asking for RCA.

james (prod-support): Customer update: sent follow-up confirming service restored and we'll share RCA within SLA window.

incident-bot: Incident status changed to 'resolved' at 08:37:15Z. Severity: P1, duration ~26 min, primary cause: transit provider mis-announcement of more-specific prefixes leading to cross-region misroutes and elevated tail latency.

ashley (eng-sre): I'll take incident commander for postmortem. Actions: 1) full postmortem in 72 hours, 2) add automated detection for more-specific leaks in BGP telemetry, 3) add pre-approved override policy to accelerate pin rollout next time, 4) update customer comms template.

maria (network-oncall): Action items for networking: 1) request SLA credit/RCAs from provider, 2) build guardrail to rate-limit propagation of more-specifics across our transit, 3) add playbook step to escalate to provider account team earlier.

simon (eng-platform): Platform follow-ups: add a safe-default to quickly enforce strict-pin for affected regions and an automated canary strategy. Will open tickets.

leo (infra): I'll gather traceroute + BGP dumps and attach to postmortem.

customer-success: Notifying affected enterprise customers now with resolution note + hold for PM for follow-up meeting.

james (prod-support): Closing loop with support cases — marking as resolved.

ashley (eng-sre): Thanks team. If anyone has additional logs, drop into #incidents-docs/1832109876. I'll start the postmortem draft.

maria (network-oncall): Handoff: I'm off in 30m, but monitoring alerts will be on-call team. Leaving follow-up notes in the ticket.

ops-runbooks-bot: Reminder: create P1 postmortem doc and link to ticket within 72h.

incident-bot: Thread archived at 08:39:59Z.

(END OF THREAD)
